phase_calls.stage_reason: Late, not mid. For six weeks in a row, the share of stocks above their 200-day average fell, from 72% to under 50%. The gains now come from one trade, not a whole sector. Big investors have cut their stock holdings three weeks running.
phase_calls.reason: The index is near its highs, but fewer stocks are doing the lifting. Under 50% of S&P 500 stocks are above their 200-day average, while the index sits above its rising one. The gains come from memory chips and AI infrastructure. Junk bonds and the VIX both look calm. Prices rising on a shrinking base, with no fear priced in, is the framework's Distribution phase.
evidence: For a second week, under 50% of S&P 500 stocks were above their 200-day average, while the index ended flat. That is the Stage 3 pattern: an index held up by fewer and fewer stocks.
Memory chips and AI infrastructure kept leading ahead of Micron's Sep 30 results. The Dow fell, and the average stock lagged the index.
Junk bonds paid 270 basis points over Treasuries, and the VIX stayed under 15. Neither bond nor stock markets are pricing a downturn, which rules out Stage 4 on this data.
phase_calls.falsifier: An S&P 500 close below its 200-day average, with under 45% of stocks above theirs and junk bonds over 300 basis points, means Contraction. Over 60% of stocks back above theirs, with small caps rising too, means Expansion. Either breaks two of the four conditions below.
